Touch Bar Simulator - Use the Touch Bar on any Mac.

summary.one_liner: A macOS app that runs the Touch Bar simulator as a standalone window on any Mac, without needing Xcode; it is discontinued because recent macOS changes broke it.
summary.what_it_does: Launches a Touch Bar simulator window from anywhere, without requiring Xcode to be installed. The window includes a transparency slider and a screenshot button. A menu bar icon toggles the window with a click or keyboard shortcut, and a system service is also provided for toggling. Right-clicking or option-clicking the menu bar icon opens options to dock the window to the top or bottom of the screen, show it on all desktops, use toolbar features in docked mode, auto show/hide the Touch Bar, or quit. Screenshots are saved to the Desktop or the clipboard via key combinations. The README says the app was rebuilt to communicate with the Touch Bar simulator directly, instead of bundling Xcode's private frameworks.
use_cases: Previewing Touch Bar layouts without a Touch Bar hardware Mac
Testing Touch Bar app interfaces without launching Xcode
Capturing screenshots of the Touch Bar
Keeping a simulated Touch Bar docked on screen
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the project's releases page
stack: Objective-C or Swift (macOS app, inferred from macOS-only private API references)
notable: Runs without Xcode, unlike Apple's built-in Touch Bar simulator that only launches from inside Xcode
Screenshot shortcuts save to Desktop (⇧⌘6) or clipboard (⌃⇧⌘6)
Menu bar icon with docking, all-desktops display, and auto show/hide options
Earlier versions bundled private Xcode frameworks; the current version is much smaller per the README
caveats: Discontinued: the README says it no longer works because of changes in macOS
Uses private APIs, so it cannot be on the Mac App Store
Clicking inside the simulator needs Accessibility permission in System Settings
